note: DRAFT criteria for the frequency-spectrum analysis (plan v2). Not frozen: there is deliberately no criteria_v2_draft.sha256, and evaluate_plan.py reports 'no frozen hash found' until the file is copied to its final name and frozen with --freeze, which must happen before any real-data result exists. Three criteria differ from the first plan document and need Yang's agreement before freezing. F2 is a partial order (CDS and conserved non-coding each above enhancers, every constrained tier above neutral) instead of a strict four-step chain, because the relative per-site constraint of CDS and phastCons non-coding elements is not established; that contrast is reported but not a criterion. F3 tests flatness of the adjusted singleton share across mutability bins on neutral sequence instead of 'spectrum shape does not predict de novo mutations': the expected spectrum itself must depend on mutability (recurrent mutation lowers the singleton share at mutable sites), so only the adjusted residual can be free of it; the de novo AUC of P(singleton | variant) is reported descriptively. F5 compares predictive log-likelihood of the frequency class on neutral sequence (a proper scoring rule) instead of the size of the constraint gradient, because a biased adjustment can produce a larger gradient. The model is trained and calibrated on mask AB (unannotated and outside phastCons elements padded by 100 bp), not on mask A as in v1, because mask A still contains conserved sequence without annotation; T1, T1v and T2 are checked on mask AB. T1 checks the conditional class shares (oe_share), which is what the calibration fits and what the scores use; the unconditional per-class ratio (oe_marginal) also depends on how P(variant) and the class distribution co-vary, is not guaranteed by the calibration, and is reported as a diagnostic only. T3 (label agreement with bcftools, per class) is a stop rule checked by hand from results/validation, as in v1. Paths are relative to the results directory; {half}, {bin}, {cls} and {seed} expand over 'over'.

criteria.claim: Coding sequence: singleton share exceeds the mutability-adjusted neutral expectation (oe_share singleton, lower 95% bound > 1)
Constraint gradient: CDS above neutral (paired difference of oe_share singleton, lower 95% bound > 0)
Constraint gradient: conserved non-coding (phastCons outside CDS) above neutral
Constraint gradient: conserved non-coding above enhancers
Separation from mutation rate: on neutral sequence the adjusted singleton share is flat across the ten mutability bins (oe_share singleton in 0.95-1.05 in every bin)
P(variant) still predicts de novo mutations: AUC (Icelandic DNMs) at most 0.01 below the original OVEP model (paired DeLong lower 95% bound)
The network predicts the neutral frequency spectrum better than the trinucleotide table: gain in -log P(class | variant) per variant on neutral sequence, lower 95% bound > 0
Class calibration on the training-neutral mask (AB): for each class, observed variants / expected given where variants were observed (oe_share) in 0.95-1.05
Variant-site calibration on the training-neutral mask (AB) (the v1 criterion S1): observed/expected in 0.95-1.05
Singleton share on the training-neutral mask (AB) matches the expectation (oe_share singleton in 0.95-1.05)
Seeds: the CDS singleton excess (oe_share singleton > 1) holds for at least 4 of 5 single-seed models
